skill.name: web-design-guidelines

content.user_title: Improve Web Interfaces with Practical Design Reviews
content.value_statement: Inconsistent interfaces can hide actions, weaken accessibility, and fail on smaller screens. This skill provides focused design decisions and evidence-based review guidance.
actual_capabilities: Review screen hierarchy, grouping, and primary actions against the user flow.
Recommend purposeful color, typography, spacing, radius, border, and elevation tokens.
Evaluate loading, empty, error, success, and stale states for continuity.
Assess keyboard order, focus visibility, modal behavior, contrast, and status feedback.
Check realistic labels, data, touch targets, text zoom, and narrow-screen layouts.
Produce concrete findings with user impact and proposed repairs.
limitations: It does not implement HTML, CSS, or JavaScript changes.
It cannot measure rendered behavior without access to the relevant screen or code.
It does not replace formal accessibility testing with assistive technology.
Recommendations depend on the product brief, existing conventions, and available evidence.

use_cases.title: Review a product screen
use_cases.description: Identify hierarchy, interaction, accessibility, and responsive issues in an existing screen or flow.

use_cases.title: Shape a visual system
use_cases.description: Create coherent roles for color, typography, spacing, borders, elevation, motion, and supported themes.

use_cases.title: Audit a responsive workflow
use_cases.description: Test realistic states and content across keyboard, pointer, touch, narrow-screen, and zoom scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner screen review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this screen for hierarchy, action clarity, accessibility, and responsive risks. List each issue, its user impact, and one practical repair.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use with a screenshot, screen description, or rendered page.

prompt_templates.title: Improve interaction states
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this flow for loading, empty, error, success, stale, focus, and recovery states. Identify missing states and propose concise interface behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a workflow feels incomplete or confusing.

prompt_templates.title: Define a visual system
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a focused visual-system proposal for this product. Define semantic color, typography, spacing, radius, border, elevation, and motion roles that match its brand and content.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a new theme or repeated visual inconsistencies.

prompt_templates.title: Conduct an evidence-based audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the affected screen and code against the product brief. Separate measured defects from preferences, cite locations, rank impact, and give verification steps for keyboard, touch, responsive, zoom, and reduced motion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced design or accessibility review.

output_examples.input: Review a checkout form with a low-contrast secondary action and no visible focus state.
output_examples.output: Finding: Keyboard users may lose track of the active field, while the secondary action is difficult to read. Repair: add a visible focus treatment and verify text and control contrast against the actual background.

output_examples.input: Create theme guidance for a dashboard that supports light and dark modes.
output: Define surface, text, border, accent, and status roles before mapping them to components.
Verify contrast in both themes and pair status colors with icons or text.
Use shared spacing and motion roles so related screens remain consistent.

output_examples.input: Audit a table workflow for narrow screens and long labels.
output_examples.output: Finding: Long labels can create accidental page overflow and obscure table context. Repair: preserve intentional table scrolling, test realistic content, and provide a clear way to return to the active filter state.

best_practices: Start with the product brief, affected screen, existing conventions, and intended interaction.
Report concrete user impact and proposed repairs, separating measured defects from preferences.
Verify representative states with keyboard, pointer or touch, realistic content, and relevant viewport sizes.
anti_patterns: Do not force a redesign or new component library for a focused repair.
Do not treat ARIA attributes as proof of accessible interaction.
Do not add dark mode, confirmation dialogs, or decorative tokens without a demonstrated need.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews hierarchy, interaction states, visual systems, responsiveness, accessibility, and user impact across screens or flows.

faq.question: Can it write frontend code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design decisions, review findings, and repair guidance. HTML, CSS, and JavaScript implementation are separate tasks.

faq.question: Can it review a screenshot?
faq.answer: Yes. A screenshot supports visual review, while code and rendered states provide stronger evidence for behavior and accessibility.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify risks, but keyboard, assistive technology, contrast, zoom, and device testing remain necessary.

faq.question: When should I use the reference design system?
faq.answer: Use it for theme creation or repeated visual inconsistencies after checking the existing tokens and components.

faq.question: What information improves the review?
faq.answer: Provide the product brief, affected screen or flow, relevant code, target devices, supported themes, and the behavior to verify.
